cases.note: intentional mutant deviation; demonstrates replay-case production, not a production counterexample

mutants.simulated_error: graph names are dropped before canonicalization, so exports differing only in graph position collapse (wrong merge)
blank identity is scoped per graph instead of per page, so a page sharing one node across graphs collapses with a page that uses distinct nodes (wrong merge)
equality is decided by stable color refinement alone without search, so locally indistinguishable non-isomorphic exports collapse (wrong merge)
blank-id strings decide which search branch defines the code ("first branch wins"), so renamed equivalent exports land separately (missed merge)

limitations: the exhaustive classification covers only the finite domain of 3 blank ids, one IRI predicate and the default graph; multi-role inputs (literals, IRI/graph roles, >3 blanks) are covered by random and constructed cases, not exhaustively

the brute-force bijection oracle is capped at 8 blank ids; larger isomorphism claims rest on explicit witness bijections, and larger non-isomorphism claims rest on specific structural certificates (K4-dichotomy), not on a general decision procedure

stress runs whose search budget is exhausted are recorded as undetermined and support no (non-)isomorphism conclusion; resource curves measured on one structure family do not extrapolate to all 32-blank inputs
random differential coverage is bounded by the recorded seed and trial count; the shrinker demonstration runs against an intentional mutant, not against production
mutants simulate four specific error classes; they cannot enumerate every possible implementation error
wall-clock times and allocation peaks are machine-dependent and only indicate orders of magnitude
